clue.text: Turner, the committee leader, allows invalid motion

definitions.note: a describing phrase: the thing that lets a disabled person move about

parts.note: a wheel is something that turns, so it is a turner
the chair is the person presiding over a committee

explanation.surface: A painter, now heading a committee, is graciously permitting an unusual proposal to be tabled.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter and 'invalid motion' like a faulty proposal at the meeting; in fact 'invalid' is the old word for a disabled person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair on wheels is the device that lets someone unable to walk get around.

clue.text: You will suffer in the heat

definitions.meaning: the archaic second-person form, as used with 'thou' in old texts and the Bible
plants droop and flag when it is hot

explanation.surface: A warning that someone is going to have a hard time in hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the archaic 'thou wilt', meaning 'you will'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic second-person form of 'will' as in 'thou wilt', and to droop or flag as flowers do in hot sun.

clue.text: Maddened avenger gives chase

indicators.note: something maddened is driven wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A furious avenger sets off in pursuit of their quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chase' looks like pursuit, but it is the metalworker's sense: to chase metal is to decorate it by cutting into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In metalwork, chasing is cutting a design into a surface, the same as incising it.

clue.text: Mercy from Caesar for Bohemia?

parts.note: Julius Caesar spoke and wrote Latin, so words from him are Latin
to give quarter is to show mercy to a defeated enemy

explanation.surface: A question about whether Caesar showed clemency towards a central European region.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemia here is not the region but bohemian life: the Latin Quarter of Paris is famous for its artists and students.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris district on the Left Bank is the classic home of artists and free-living bohemians, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Poet to indicate complicity in trick

parts.note: Thomas Hood was a nineteenth-century English poet
a wink signals that you are in on a secret

explanation.surface: A poet signals a shared secret while taking part in a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or fool someone, synonym.

clue.text: Arch no different from others

definitions.meaning: the arched middle part of the foot
marching in time with everyone else, conforming

explanation.surface: A remark that some arch is just like all the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised curve of the foot between toes and ankle, and the idiom for being in time and conforming with everybody else.

clue.text: Vegetable root cutter

definitions.meaning: a narrow spade or chisel-like tool for digging out weeds by the root

explanation.surface: A vegetable described by the tool used to slice roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a potato, and a small digging tool used to cut through weed roots.

clue.text: Keep going for pine

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: An instruction to persevere for the sake of some pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree but is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend or keep something going for longer, synonym.

clue.text: Bowl — sort of ware not hard to discourage

parts.note: a dish is a bowl

indicators.note: 'not hard' asks for the letter for hard to be taken away

parts.note: earthenware is a type of pottery, so earthen is a sort of ware
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A pottery bowl that is not hard enough is disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H (hard) from EARTHEN, leaving EARTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispirit someone or take away their confidence, synonym.

clue.text: Easy to accommodate Mrs Woolf's aim

definitions.note: Virginia Woolf's novel To the Lighthouse names its characters' destination

parts.note: a light task is an easy one
to house someone is to accommodate them

explanation.surface: Saying it is simple to put up Virginia Woolf for her purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia Woolf wrote To the Lighthouse; the family in it spend the novel aiming to sail there.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Woolf's novel names the tower on the coast that the family set out towards.

clue.text: The Allies' first battle — only half a Frenchman left?

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, here its first four of eight letters

parts.note: monsieur is the French title for a man

explanation.surface: After the first Allied battle, only half a Frenchman remains standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons, in Belgium, was the British Expeditionary Force's first battle of the First World War in August 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian town gave its name to the first British battle of 1914.

clue.text: Survive test, being well covered

parts.note: to weather a storm is to survive it
a proof is a test, as in 'the proof of the pudding'

explanation.surface: Coming through an examination because one is well protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Protected against rain and wind, so well sheltered.

clue.text: Sounds exhausted but alert

indicators.note: this word signals that what is heard, not what is written, gives the letters

parts.note: worn out means exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone sounds tired yet still on the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone is to give notice of danger, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Miserable? Cheer up!

definitions.meaning: split into three words, it is a command for sorrow to depart

explanation.surface: A question followed by an encouraging exclamation to a gloomy friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Means looking downcast and sad, and, split into three words, wishes that sorrow be banished.

clue.text: Later, when peace returns, have two children

parts.note: peace returns after war
D is daughter and S is son, two children

explanation.surface: A promise that once peace comes back, the couple will start a family of two.
explanation.definitionFit: At a subsequent time, synonym.

clue.text: Common haunt

explanation.surface: A ghost that is a regular presence.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring often, adjective; and to visit a place habitually, verb.

clue.text: Old actor — where he may make his entrance?

definitions.meaning: a veteran performer of long experience, as in the idiom with 'old'

definitions.text: where he may make his entrance?
definitions.meaning: read as a platform plus R for right, it names the side of the boards from which a player comes on

explanation.surface: A veteran actor wonders which wing he will enter from.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as STAGE R: stage right, one of the sides from which an actor comes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran performer, as in 'old stager'; and cryptically the stage-right side where an actor enters.

clue.text: Hole-in-the-middle mint?

definitions.meaning: the centre ring of a target
a hard round peppermint sweet popular in Britain

explanation.surface: A peppermint with a hole through its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The central circle of a dartboard or target, and a striped British boiled peppermint sweet.

clue.text: Date the Cortes was dissolved

indicators.note: something dissolved breaks up, so these letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Asking when the Spanish parliament was disbanded.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cortes is the Spanish parliament; 'Date' looks like a request for a year but is a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner taken out for the evening, a companion.

clue.text: Go out with a nice invention

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes a nice person out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' works on GO and A NICE together, with 'with' as the link word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly made-up word or phrase is a coinage, something invented.

clue.text: In a train, love comes to blossom

indicators.note: In places one word inside the other

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground train
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Romance flowers on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container; 'a train' is the London Underground, and 'blossom' is the definition, not a verb: the tuberose is a fragrant white-flowered plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant white-flowered plant grown for perfume, so a kind of flower.

clue.text: Available to discuss outside

parts.note: open means available
to air a matter is to discuss it publicly

explanation.surface: Someone is willing to talk things over out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of doors, not indoors, synonym.

clue.text: Does it encourage vehicle corrosion?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
rot is decay or corrosion

explanation.surface: A question about whether something speeds up rust on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the vegetable dangled before a donkey is an incentive, while its two parts describe rusting cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial incentive held out before a donkey, as in carrot and stick, encourages.

clue.text: Innocent king left the scene of another king's death

definitions.text: the scene of another king's death

parts.note: white suggests purity and innocence
Hal is the name for Henry V as prince in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A guiltless monarch departed from where another ruler died.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I was beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall, London, in 1649.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles I was executed on a scaffold in the London street in 1649.

clue.text: Mouse to owl: I beg you to listen

indicators.note: these words ask the solver to hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: pray is the old way of saying please, I beg you

explanation.surface: A mouse pleads with an owl to hear it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The mouse's plea to the owl is apt: it is the owl's quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a creature an owl hunts, its quarry.

clue.text: River, sacred and nearly the best

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: alpha, the first Greek letter, marks the best grade

explanation.surface: A holy river that is almost the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan opens 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy stream in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan.

clue.text: Sound of Bottom's nightingale, or the sea on Dover Beach

definitions.meaning: Bottom in A Midsummer Night's Dream promises to bellow as gently as any nightingale
Matthew Arnold's poem Dover Beach hears the grating noise of pebbles flung by waves

explanation.surface: A literary question about the noise made by Shakespeare's weaver and by Arnold's sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom the weaver says 'I will roar you an 'twere any nightingale'; Arnold writes of 'the grating roar of pebbles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom's boast in Shakespeare and Arnold's line about pebbles both use this word for a loud bellow.

clue.text: A fight to get other ranks into earth orbit

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a satellite in orbit is in continuous free fall around the earth
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A space race in which ordinary soldiers are launched into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container. An orbiting craft is weightless because it is constantly falling round the earth, which is why 'earth orbit' gives the piece it does.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly brawl in which everyone joins, a melee.

clue.text: Made late by enforced turn

definitions.meaning: the late is the deceased, so made late means killed
to swing or twist round forcibly

explanation.surface: Someone was delayed by a compulsory detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, as in 'the late king', so 'made late' is killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of slay, killed; and to swing round, as a vehicle skids sideways.

clue.text: Run into the forest, mistaken for betrayer of Little Em'ly

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other
mistaken means wrong, so these letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone runs into the woods in error, taken for a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges THE FOREST, and 'into' puts R inside. In Dickens's David Copperfield, Steerforth seduces Little Em'ly.
explanation.definitionFit: In David Copperfield, the charming seducer elopes with Little Em'ly and abandons her.
